Ah, you're absolutely right! I had that backwards. `COUNT(email)` only counts non-NULL values in that column, so it returned 980. `COUNT(*)` counts all rows regardless of NULL values, which would give you 1000. 

So the 20-row difference tells you exactly what you found: 20 users in your table have a NULL email address. That's a useful way to spot data gaps like missing email values.
